findings.title: AWS access key ID hardcoded and committed to the repository
findings.evidence: The added line assigns a literal AWS access key ID to a module-level constant: 'AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID = "[REDACTED-AWS-KEY]"'. Any user with read access to ops/deploy.py (or to repo history once merged) obtains a live credential. Removing it in a later commit does not remediate it because the value persists in git history, so the key must be treated as compromised.
findings.recommendation: Delete the constant and rotate/revoke the exposed key immediately. Load credentials from the standard boto3 chain (AWS_PROFILE / environment variables / IAM instance role) or from a secrets manager at runtime; add a secret-scanning pre-commit hook (e.g. gitleaks/detect-secrets) and purge the value from history before merging.

findings.title: Module-level credential constant is never used by the boto3 client
findings.evidence: The credential is stored in a plain module constant 'AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID = ...' but the following 'client = boto3.client("s3", region_name=REGION)' call passes no credentials and does not read module globals; boto3 resolves credentials from env vars, shared config, or instance metadata. So the line leaks a secret while having no effect on authentication — either the intended auth is silently not happening (deploy uses ambient credentials or fails with NoCredentialsError), or it is dead code.
findings.recommendation: Remove the constant. If explicit credentials are genuinely required, use boto3.Session(aws_access_key_id=..., aws_secret_access_key=...) sourcing both values from environment/secrets store, and fail fast with a clear error when the secret key is missing; add a test asserting the client is built from configuration rather than hardcoded literals.
